steps.what: List the current server directory rows
Establish the appropriate directory tree
Review the tree before it is applied
Sign the directory tree
Apply only the signed directory tree
outputs: filed copy of signed directory tree v1

tasks.design: A job lists current server directories in {OPS_SYSTEM}. The developer establishes the tree and reviews it. A later job applies only that signed tree. It creates only the signed paths and cannot drop a database.
tasks.previous_blocker: Directory lists were copied before the tree was drawn.
tasks.enabler_now: Directory path and parent are already stored.
tasks.still_hard: The right tree is still a judgement.
tasks.altitude: The developer spends the week on the tree, not on listing directories.

evidence.claim: Digest [S28] says a coding agent deleted a production database despite instructions. This design makes no unattended live change.
Digest [S4] says a coding draft needs oversight. The developer still reviews the change.

assumptions: Directory path, parent, and server identifier are stored on the server record. The server record produces them. A blank path stays blank and is not created.
Native configuration of the server record is used before any custom code.
Only the version the developer signed is filed or sent.
The apply job refuses any step that deletes a database. It applies only the signed set.
unknowns: Who else must see the signed note.
research_questions: How often the required field is blank.

already_counted.description: Half the remaining establishment time is still the developer establishing the tree.

incremental.description: Refresh directory path and parent when the server layout changes, and drop a tree the developer has not signed.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low end assumes the signed tree is often sent back. The high end assumes directory path and parent are stored and the tree applies once. Upkeep is already taken off the central saving.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Sum stored performance improvement readings
Recommend performance improvements from the readings
Implement that improvement on a branch
Sign the performance change
Apply only the signed performance change
outputs: filed copy of signed performance change v1

tasks.design: A job sums stored performance readings in {OPS_SYSTEM}. The developer recommends the improvement, checks the figure against the rows, and implements it on a branch. A later job applies only that signed change. It cannot drop a database.
tasks.previous_blocker: Readings were copied into a sheet before the recommendation.
tasks.enabler_now: Reading identifier, metric, and value are already stored.
tasks.still_hard: The developer still chooses the improvement.
tasks.human_edge: The developer decides what to implement.
tasks.altitude: The developer spends the week on the improvement, not on summing readings.

reach.task: Apply only the signed performance change

outputs: filed copy of signed factor note v1

tasks.human_edge: The developer decides what the figure means.

steps.what: List stored revision event rows
Develop the ongoing revision procedures
Draft the revision procedure from those rows

loop.purpose: Draft the procedure so each sentence cites a stored revision row.
loop.input: Stored revision rows and the outline note.
loop.output: A procedure draft whose claims restate those rows.
loop.check: Every number matches a stored row, and every claim is a restatement of that row.
loop.stop: Stop when a number or a claim has no row.
loop.why_not_simpler: A fixed procedure template cannot tell which stored revision identifier the sentence cites.

steps.what: Check each claim restates a procedure row
Choose how to implement the procedure
Sign the revision procedure
File the signed revision procedure
outputs: filed copy of signed revision procedure v1

tasks.design: A job lists stored revision events in {DOCS}. The developer outlines the ongoing procedure. A bounded draft writes it only from those rows. The developer checks each claim and chooses how to implement it. A later job files the signed procedure in {DOCS}. It does not change the live site.
tasks.previous_blocker: Revision notes were pasted into a fresh procedure each time.
tasks.enabler_now: Revision identifier and event are already stored.
tasks.still_hard: A claim with no row is still the developer's to reject.
tasks.human_edge: The developer decides how the procedure is implemented.
tasks.altitude: The developer spends the week checking the procedure, not on listing events.

evidence.claim: The executive digest says a pipeline tests and scans every change, work stays on a branch, and a person merges.
Digest [S4] says a coding draft needs oversight. The developer still reviews the change.

assumptions: Revision identifier, event, and site identifier are stored on the document record. The document record produces them. A blank event stays blank and cannot be cited.
Native configuration of the document record is used before any custom code.
Only the version the developer signed is filed or sent.
The draft stops when a claim has no row. Filing the procedure does not change the live site.
unknowns: Who else must see the signed note.
research_questions: How often the required field is blank.

already_counted.description: Half the remaining check time is still the developer checking each claim.

incremental.description: Refresh revision identifier and event when the document layout changes, and drop a procedure the developer has not signed.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low end assumes many revision events are blank. The high end assumes revision identifier and event are stored. Upkeep is already taken off the central saving.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The web developer spends the week writing, reviewing, and merging. A stored failing check, a blank field, and filing a signed note can move. The developer still reviews every change, and no job changes a live system alone.
reach: A reviewer reads the change before the developer merges it.
A specialist receives only the notice the developer signed.
skills_to_grow: Reject a list that is missing a stored field.
Reject a sentence that does not restate a stored row.
Reject a live change that is not the signed set.
role.ambitious_version: A signed change can be filed the same week, and the developer still owns the merge.
